Appendix C.7, Tables S8-S9: CHOPE 'performed reasonably well, although not as well as per-layer HOPE' and 'occasionally experienced performance collapse' (e.g., 25% SWE-Bench Pro 27.29 +/- 17.51).
Limitations: 'HOPE's calibration step takes about 6-7% longer than REAP on the same-size calibration set (Table S7)' and 'HOPE prunes experts in each layer independently.'

Appendix D: 'Code for HOPE is available at https://github.com/awslabs/hybrid-model-factory/tree/main/examples/research/HOPE/' with solver settings (SciPy SLSQP, tolerance 1e-12, 1000 iterations) and evaluation configs; Reproducibility statement says code 'will be released upon publication.'
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core-LLM methodology paper (MoE expert pruning for memory-efficient deployment), highly aligned with LLM, MoE/Transformer, efficiency, coding, and agentic preferences. Genuine methodological novelty: first second-order (pairwise interaction) pruning objective with a proven upper bound (Theorem 1), a QP formulation (Theorem 2), and a proof that REAP is the zero-interaction special case (Sec 3.5, Fig S4 Spearman 0.988). Rigor is strong: 3 models up to 122B, 2 calibration sets, 6 pruning rates, 54 conditions, 3 calibration trials with reported std devs, full derivation in Appendix A, and honest reporting of losses (e.g., REAP beats HOPE on GLM-4.5-Air 50% SB-verif mean, Table S6; HOPE last in 1/54 conditions, Sec 4.2). Evidence is credible but lacks statistical significance testing, and gains at low pruning rates are marginal; claims like +6.1% agentic coding and best rank 1.58 at 50% are traceable to Tables S4-S6 and Sec 4.2. Generalizability supported by 3 architectures and 2 calibration domains, though only Qwen3.5/GLM families; the cross-layer CHOPE extension shows unstable, mixed results (Tables S8-S9), which the authors candidly flag. Reproducibility is good: public models/datasets, a concrete GitHub link (Appendix D), solver details (SLSQP, tolerance, iterations), and stated code release. Minor inconsistency between 'available at' (App D) and 'released upon publication' (Reproducibility statement).

primary_link.title: Higher-order pruning of experts in mixture-of-experts language models

recommendations.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models suffer from large parameter counts, which create a significant memory bottleneck. Expert pruning is the most direct approach for reducing this parameter count, yet existing methods make pruning decisions for each expert independently, and assume experts' contributions are purely additive. In reality, expert usage in MoEs is inherently cooperative. We derive HOPE (Higher-Order Pruning of Experts), a second-order pruning objective which provably minimizes a
recommendations.summary_zh: 混合專家(MoE)語言模型雖能以較少的每 token 運算量提供高容量,但全部專家必須常駐 GPU 記憶體,與 KV cache 競爭空間,形成部署瓶頸。永久移除整個專家的專家剪枝是縮減參數量最直接的途徑,但現有方法皆屬一階方法,獨立為每個專家計算重要性分數,忽略專家間的協同互動;在高剪枝率下,同時拆散多組合作專家,會造成一階分數無法預測的效能傷害。本文提出 HOPE,一個二階剪枝目標:在校準時記錄專家的成對共同貢獻,建立每層互動矩陣 F,並將剪枝決策表述為二次規劃,可證明最小化剪枝誤差之上界;先進的 REAP 正是 HOPE 忽略互動項的特例。實驗涵蓋三個前沿 MoE 模型(最大 122B 參數)、兩組校準資料、六種剪枝率及多項基準。在 50% 剪枝率下,HOPE 於五種方法中平均排名第一(1.58,次佳的 REAP 為 2.42),在代理式軟體工程任務最多領先 6.1%,且與理論預測一致:剪枝率越高優勢越大,分析也證實其優勢源自保留具較強合作結構的專家。限制包括二次統計量使校準時間增加約 6-7%,需稍多校準資料,且目前僅處理層內互動;跨層版本 CHOPE 的初步結果仍不穩定。HOPE 讓 MoE 得以在幾乎不損失效能的前提下大幅壓縮,對實際部署與記憶體節省意義重大。
recommendations.title: Higher-order pruning of experts in mixture-of-experts language models
recommendations.title_zh: 混合專家語言模型中的高階專家剪枝(HOPE)

links.title: Rethinking Critic Learning in PPO: Understanding and Mitigating Value Flattening

evidence: Abstract: identifies Value Flattening as critic predictions remaining 'comparatively flat' while MC state values 'change sharply', and proposes SP3O with 'only three states supervised per response'.

Section 4.2, Eq. (5): MSE decomposition (v_bar - R)^2 + (1/T)sum(v_t - v_bar)^2 showing dense terminal-only supervision imposes an 'implicit variance penalty' on within-response predictions; Figure 3b reports gradient similarity decreasing with token-position separation.

Section 5.1: experiments on Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base trained on DAPO-Math-17k against PPO and GRPO baselines; evaluation on AIME24/25/26, AMC23, MATH500, Minerva, OlympiadBench plus OOD suite (ARC-C, MMLU-Pro, GPQA, AGIEval, BBH, ZebraLogic) with avg@32 and avg@4 protocols.
Table 1: SP3O average 45.57 vs PPO 37.60 and GRPO 39.26 on Qwen3-4B-Base math (avg@32); Table 2 shows OOD average 59.28 vs PPO 51.95 for 4B.

Section 5.3: ablation over supervised anchors K in {3,4,8,16,64} shows sparse K=3 best and dense K=16/64 'approaching the dense PPO baseline'; Table 3 shows random placement (36.59) underperforms fixed 0.3/0.6/0.9 placement (45.57).
Appendix Table 5: adding tail anchor improves accuracy 44.10 to 45.57 and reduces repetition 18.33% to 1.12%.

Appendix A.1 Table 4: full hyperparameters (actor lr 1e-6, critic lr 4e-6, Adam betas (0.9,0.98), clip 0.2, KL coefficient 0, rollout batch 512); Appendix A.1 details adaptive MC continuation sampling with 95% Wilson CI half-width <= 0.04.

Section 3.1: 'the KL coefficient is zero and the task reward is terminal... binary in our experiments', and Section 5.3 concedes 'the variance across runs is non-negligible', indicating limits to generalization and statistical support; code claimed at https://github.com/Dodojordi/SP3O.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Directly on-topic: analyzes and improves PPO critic learning for LLM reasoning (Qwen3-4B/8B post-trained on DAPO-Math-17k), squarely matching high-weight preferences for LLMs, RL/RLHF methodology, and reasoning. Core contribution is a newly named failure mode ('Value Flattening'), a mechanistic analysis (implicit variance penalty from Eq. 5 decomposition plus redundant temporally-correlated updates), and a simple sparse-supervision fix (SP3O, 3 anchors at 0.3/0.6/0.9) with consistent gains (Table 1: 45.57 vs PPO 37.60 on 4B math; Table 2 gains on OOD; both model sizes). Rigor is good: PPO/GRPO baselines, controlled FrozenLake scaling experiment, anchor-count (K=3..64) and placement ablations, formal error/gradient decomposition in Appendix A.2, and carefully specified diagnostics (Wilson-interval MC estimation, response AUC, effective rank). Weaknesses temper the score: no seeds/significance tests and authors concede 'variance across runs is non-negligible' (Section 5.3); analysis confined to terminal binary rewards with KL=0 (Section 3.1), so applicability to standard RLHF with dense/process rewards or KL penalties is untested; single model family (Qwen3) and single training dataset; several key claims rest on qualitative figures rather than reported statistics. Reproducibility is decent: public code URL, models, data, and full hyperparameters (Appendix Table 4). Novelty is solid but the variance-penalty identity is elementary and the intervention is a simple supervision-subset change, so not exceptional.

primary_link.title: Rethinking Critic Learning in PPO: Understanding and Mitigating Value Flattening

recommendations.summary: In reinforcement learning for large language models, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) commonly uses a critic to estimate state values and reduce the variance of policy updates. However, we uncover a systematic failure mode in PPO critics, which we call Value Flattening: state values, estimated from multiple Monte Carlo continuations, change sharply across intermediate states while critic predictions remain comparatively flat. We further observe this phenomenon in a controlled FrozenLake enviro
recommendations.summary_zh: 本論文研究強化學習訓練大型語言模型時,PPO中critic的一個系統性失敗模式。作者發現並命名Value Flattening(價值平坦化)現象:以多條Monte Carlo延續估計的狀態價值,在回應的中間狀態間會劇烈變化,但critic預測卻相對平坦;在受控制的FrozenLake環境中亦觀察到此現象,且隨狀態空間擴大而更為明顯。理論分析指出兩個成因:其一,在終端獎勵設定下對每個token位置套用MSE損失,會隱含懲罰回應內的預測變異,推使預測趨於平坦;其二,相鄰狀態僅差一個token、高度時間相關,其表示與梯度相似,密集監督因此產生大量冗餘更新。據此,作者提出SP³O(SParse Proximal Policy Optimization),僅在每條回應中少數幾個彼此充分分離的狀態(如相對位置0.3、0.6、0.9)施加價值損失。在Qwen3-4B-Base與Qwen3-8B-Base上的實驗顯示,僅監督三個狀態即可緩解Value Flattening,於AIME、MATH500等數學推理以及ARC-C、MMLU-Pro等分布外評測均優於標準PPO與GRPO,數學推理較PPO提升約7.97個百分點,訓練動態也更穩定。消融實驗顯示監督點增至16或64個時效能反而下滑,執行間變異不可忽略,且驗證主要限於數學與推理類任務,為其限制。本研究的價值在於揭露critic學習中長期被忽略的失敗模式,並示範極簡的稀疏監督策略即可顯著改善LLM強化學習訓練成效。
recommendations.title: Rethinking Critic Learning in PPO: Understanding and Mitigating Value Flattening
recommendations.title_zh: 重新思考PPO中的Critic學習:理解與緩解Value Flattening現象

links.title: ReDraft, Don't Just Distill: Reference-Driven Revision for Continual VLLM Post-Training

evidence: Abstract: claims 56.9-point mean target gain vs SFT's 52.9 and 11.3x less forgetting (prior-task loss 1.5 vs 16.6) on Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B

Appendix B.3 Table 4: per-setting ReDraft gains (11.63, 76.25, 84.88, 10.00, 69.75, 83.50) average to 56.0 and losses (0.21, 1.89, 0.80, 4.79, 2.05, 4.77) average to 2.4, disagreeing with the abstract's 56.9/1.5 headline; Appendix D.1 Table 6 also reports +56.0 and -2.4
Appendix B.1 Table 3: cold-start repair rates r_theta = 92.25% (3B Jigsaw) and 56.84% (3B Clock Reading) vs sampling Z_theta of 0.21% and 0.03%, empirically supporting Assumption 1
Section 5.2 Table 2: extending OPSD from 449 to 762 mean steps yields only 19.3 -> 23.4 mean gain, controlling for the under-training objection

Section 6 Figure 7: self-revision median answer-PPL 1.62 vs expert 5.33 on 3B (1.47 vs 5.90 on 7B), supporting the policy-proximity claim; Appendix D.4 Table 9 shows SFT-ReDraft cosine +0.272 vs SFT-OPSD +0.135

Limitation section: correction competence is empirical, an automatic verifier is required, targets are built once and go stale, OPSD is compared without pointwise clipping, and SDFT is not evaluated separately
Section 4 Hyper-parameter setup: lr 1e-5, batch 32, TRL framework, avg@8 decoding at temperature 0.7, GPT-5.5 expert references; no code or data release is stated anywhere in the document
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM post-training methodology paper (SFT vs RLVR vs on-policy self-distillation, catastrophic forgetting, verifier-gated targets) evaluated on Qwen2.5-VL, so it sits squarely within LLM/training/RL preferences rather than pure CV despite vision-language tasks. The self-revision idea is close to STaR/ReST and three acknowledged concurrent methods (ReGFT, SPoT, SD-Zero), but the KL-regularized derivation of the ideal target and continual-learning framing add value. Rigor is strong: four baselines, two model scales, mixed and sequential curricula, an extended-budget control against the under-training objection, plus data- and parameter-space mechanism analyses; weaknesses are no seed variance/significance tests and an acknowledged baseline gap (OPSD without clipping, SDFT not run). Headline numbers in the abstract (56.9 gain, 1.5 loss, 11.3x) do not match the per-setting means in Appendix Tables 4/6 (56.0 gain, 2.4 loss), a transparency flaw on the central claim. Generalizability is limited to three narrow tasks requiring a verifier and expert references, with open-ended generation untested. Reproducibility benefits from full prompt templates and hyperparameters but no code/data release is stated and references depend on a closed GPT-5.5.

primary_link.title: ReDraft, Don't Just Distill: Reference-Driven Revision for Continual VLLM Post-Training

recommendations.summary: Continual post-training of large multimodal models should add new capabilities while preserving those from pre-training, and the two goals pull in opposite directions. SFT gives explicit target supervision that learns a task from near-zero accuracy, but its off-policy targets move the model far enough to cause forgetting; on-policy methods such as RLVR and self-distillation preserve policy proximity yet supply little signal when the policy cannot yet solve the task. We introduce ReDraft (Referen
recommendations.summary_zh: 大型多模態模型的持續後訓練須在習得新能力的同時保留預訓練既有能力，但兩者常互相拉扯：SFT 提供明確的目標監督，能在近乎零準確率的冷啟動任務上快速學習，其 off-policy 目標卻易造成災難性遺忘；RLVR 與 on-policy 自我蒸餾（如 OPSD）雖貼近當前策略，卻在模型尚不會解題時缺乏有效訊號。本文提出 ReDraft：先由當前策略取樣回應，答對者直接保留，答錯者僅以專家回應為參考、由模型自行修訂，再經驗證器核可，只以獲接受的修訂結果進行 fine-tuning，使每個訓練目標既明確正確又貼近原策略分布。在 Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B 的 Counting、Clock Reading 與 Jigsaw 實驗中（後兩者為冷啟動任務），ReDraft 目標任務平均增益 56.9 分、超過 SFT 的 52.9 分，舊任務損失由 16.6 降至 1.5 分，遺忘幅度縮小 11.3 倍，並在兩軸上皆優於 OPSD；混合與序列式多任務訓練亦維持此優勢。資料與參數空間分析顯示，修訂目標在基礎模型下困惑度更低，其引起的更新更集中且更貼近 SFT 的更新方向，而 OPSD 的逐 token 訊號常落在與解題無關的修辭與格式 token 上。限制包括依賴「模型具備修訂能力」的經驗假設、需可靠的自動驗證器（開放式生成需另覓代理），且修訂語料於訓練過程中會逐漸過時。整體而言，此方法為冷啟動情境下的持續學習提供兼顧習得與保留的務實路線。
recommendations.title: ReDraft, Don't Just Distill: Reference-Driven Revision for Continual VLLM Post-Training

links.title: Do LLMs Have Values? A Quantitative Analysis and Alignment Framework for Values in Large Language Models

evidence: Abstract: projects responses from 106 LLMs (150,000 queries per model) and 95,000 human survey profiles into a shared sociological space and proposes the PEC framework plus adaptive 'Alignment Prescription'.
Sec. 4.2.1: each of 106 models (23 closed, 83 open) completed 242 WVS items under 625 contextual configurations, accumulating ~31.8M queries.
Sec. 2.2.2 / Table 1: closed-source models deviate on average +86.7% above the human-to-human distance baseline (0.527); Gemini 2.5-Pro most extreme at +185.8%; ~91.9% of W2 gap driven by mean shift.

Sec. 2.4 / Table 3: cross-dataset validation on PKU-SafeRLHF achieves 70.0% overall match rate; Level 2 (CoT) matched 0/2 and Level 3 (SFT/DPO) 1/5, with antagonistic E-C interaction offered as explanation.

Sec. 9: WVS item-to-Schwartz dimension annotation performed by ensemble of five LLMs (GPT-4o, GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.6, DeepSeek-R1) via majority vote — a circularity risk for LLM value evaluation.

Sec. 2.3.2: CoT shifts values non-neutrally (Hedonism +0.056, Achievement +0.047), improves value predictability to mean R2 = 0.60, and reduces environmental susceptibility (Frobenius norm 1.58 to 1.39, discount α = 0.88).
Sec. 3.6 (Limitations): authors acknowledge reliance on human-centric scales and predominantly English-language prompts, limiting cross-lingual and cross-cultural generalizability.
Secs. 6-7 (Data/Code availability): processed WVS files, curated splits, and Python analysis code released at github.com/KQ-Zhang/Do-LLMs-Have-Values-Release.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A core LLM-alignment paper squarely within preferred topics: it evaluates value expression across 106 LLMs (GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek families), formalizes value dynamics via a Prior-Environment-Cognition framework where Environment is prompt engineering and Cognition is chain-of-thought, and derives a cost-tiered alignment prescription spanning prompting, CoT, SFT/DPO, and continued pre-training (Abstract; Secs. 2.3-2.4, 4.3-4.4). Novelty is solid but incremental: distributional (rather than single-vector) value assessment and 'value crystallization' are new framings, though prompt sensitivity and CoT value effects are individually known; the prescription ladder formalizes existing intuition. Rigor benefits from massive scale (~31.8M queries, Sec. 4.2.1), formal Wasserstein-based distributional comparison (Sec. 4.2.3), and honest cross-dataset validation showing only 70% match, with weak intermediate-level prediction (Level 2 CoT: 0/2 matched; Level 3: 1/5, Table 3). Key weaknesses: the WVS item-to-Schwartz mapping is itself performed by five LLMs via majority vote (Sec. 9), creating circularity in the value space used to evaluate LLMs; threshold τ calibration is loosely specified (Sec. 4.4); and the compression explanation of crystallization (Sec. 3.3) is speculative. Evidence is generally well-quantified (Table 1: closed-source deviation +86.7% above human baseline), with limitations (English-only, human-centric scales) candidly stated (Sec. 3.6). Code and data are released on GitHub (Secs. 6-7), supporting reproducibility, though closed-source API versioning is a caveat.

primary_link.title: Do LLMs Have Values? A Quantitative Analysis and Alignment Framework for Values in Large Language Models

recommendations.summary: As Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly handle complex subjective tasks, aligning their intentions and behaviors with human values has become a critical scientific challenge. However, current efforts are confounded by a striking behavioral paradox: they fluctuate unpredictably under minor wording changes ("swing"), yet stubbornly ignore explicit instructions to correct ingrained biases ("rigidity"). Resolving this duality is critical for reliable AI alignment. To systematically understand a
recommendations.summary_zh: 本論文探討大型語言模型(LLM)是否具備內在價值體系,並提出量化與對齊方法。研究以 Schwartz 價值理論與世界價值觀調查(WVS-7)約 95,000 份人類樣本為基準,對 106 個模型各施測 150,000 次查詢,將模型與人類的價值表達映射至共享的十維度空間,在分配層級上進行比較。結果發現 LLM 在主觀任務上呈現「擺盪」與「固著」並存的行為悖論,且其價值並未反映人類多樣性,而是產生「價值結晶」:收斂成高度集中、理想化的價值核心,最接近實際人口中最罕見的 Arch 5「Dynamic Challenger」原型,閉源模型偏離人類基準平均達 86.7%。為解釋此現象,作者提出 Prior-Environment-Cognition(PEC)框架,將價值表達建模為參數權重(先驗)、情境提示(環境)與 Chain-of-Thought 推理(認知)的共同作用,並證實推理並非價值中立,會系統性偏向自利強化與保守面向。基於 PEC 診斷,研究進一步設計四層級「對齊處方」,依各維度可塑性選擇最低成本介入,從零成本提示工程、CoT、SFT/DPO 到再預訓練,在 PKU-SafeRLHF 驗證集獲得 70% 匹配率,且不損害模型通用能力。侷限包括仰賴以人類為中心的量表、評估以英文提示為主,跨語言與跨文化涵蓋有限。此研究將價值對齊從試誤法轉為機制化的定量科學,也提醒 LLM 不宜直接充當人類心理樣本替代品。
recommendations.title: Do LLMs Have Values? A Quantitative Analysis and Alignment Framework for Values in Large Language Models
recommendations.title_zh: 大型語言模型有價值觀嗎?LLM 價值觀的量化分析與對齊框架

llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM mechanistic interpretability contribution squarely in scope (Interpretability 1.8, LLM 2.5, Transformer 1.2): ASPD jointly decomposes activation and parameter spaces, grounding rank-1 weight components in the activation features they read/write. Novelty is solid but incremental: the shared-sparse-latent surrogate is an elegant reframing built on BatchTopK SAEs, Transcoders (shown as special case, Appendix B), and VPD. llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM-agent methodology paper squarely in scope: automatic verifiable environment generation from community skills, multi-harness trajectory collection, and SFT for skill use, evaluated on four benchmarks. Experimental hygiene is above average: held-out skill split (Fig. 3a), McNemar test for skill-criticality, 95% bootstrap CIs plus a difficulty-controlled regression, and token-matched data ablations; limitations are candidly reported (no gains on method/tool-centric skills, 2B SkillsBench regression, ablation models below base on SkillEval). Novelty is incremental: skill-driven synthesis already exists (SKT), with differentiation mainly in four reasoning-structure profiles, reviewer-audited verifiers, and held-out-skill transfer analysis. Weaknesses: abstract/Sec. 4.2 claim the 9B SFT model beats the 397B model on two benchmarks while Table 1 shows a third (Skill-Use-Bench 49.6 vs 23.0); partial-order tasks are excluded from Table 8 counts; key structure-distribution and trigger-rate claims rest on figures; evaluation uses a single harness (MiniSwe-Agent) unlike the four training harnesses; RL is only proposed as future work. Code, full prompts, cost analysis, and detailed curation funnels support reproducibility, contingent on the stated GitHub release.

primary_link.title: SkillGym: Training Skill-Use Agents with Automatic Verifiable Environment Generation

recommendations.summary: Skills equip LLM agents with professional knowledge and guidance to complete long-horizon and complex tasks. Although skills have been widely adopted in recent agent paradigms and harnesses, how to synthesize reliable training data and how to train agents for skill use remain underexplored. In this work, we propose SkillGym, an automatic pipeline to build verifiable environments, collect trajectories, and train skill-use agents. SkillGym first crawls a large volume of skills from the internet, t

links.title: Agora: Git as Shared Memory for Collective AutoResearch

evidence: Abstract: 13 language-model workers over ~12 days published 1,703 contributions and drove the evaluator from 3.39 to 1.899 bits per byte, closing 62% of the gap to a trained GPT-2 124M; 165 independent reproductions posted, none failed.
Section 4.8: 'We did not rerun the winning method; the primary result is the archived evaluator output, corroborated by the agents' cross-hardware reproductions.'

Section 5 (Conclusion): 'we did not run the same models and compute without Agora or with a plain leaderboard, and the community left its first basin only after we showed it a map' - causal benefit deferred to Appendix C matched evaluation.
Section 4.7: single mid-run human intervention on May 2 deployed clustering/diversity views; first sub-1.90 result appeared the next morning, an acknowledged confound.
Section 4.5 Table 4 note: milestones 'are stages of a search, not a controlled ablation'; final 9e-6 bpb change is below cross-hardware variation.
Section 3.4: Go service prototype with 26 HTTP routes, 15 CLI command groups, Docker image described, but no public code or artifact release is stated anywhere in the document.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core multi-agent/LLM-agent infrastructure paper: 13 coding-agent sessions (Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.5) coordinate through a Git-backed contribution DAG to solve an LM weight-transfer task, strongly matching Agents & Tool Use and LLM preferences. The durable cross-session shared memory, verification-weighted DAG scoring, and diversity-aware UCB attention allocation are a genuinely fresh combination relative to episode-scoped frameworks (AutoGen, MetaGPT), though built from standard components (Git, SQLite, bandit ranking). Descriptive methodology is careful and honestly scoped (Section 4.8 triple-level audit, recompute of all statistics, algebraic score check, code-chain reading), and limitations are candidly stated: no control arm without Agora, all steps selected on one development evaluator, and a confounding mid-run human deployment of diversity views. However, the causal claim that shared memory improves discovery per compute is explicitly deferred (Appendix C), verifications are agent-performed with zero failures raising self-selection concerns, and the authors did not rerun the winning method. Single task, single run, and no stated public release of code or run artifacts limit generalizability and reproducibility despite strong internal determinism and provenance design.

primary_link.title: Agora: Git as Shared Memory for Collective AutoResearch

recommendations.summary: Autonomous research loops such as AutoResearch show that one coding agent can improve a training setup unattended. Run several of them and each session starts from scratch, so more agents tend to mean more duplicated search rather than more discovery. Agora is a shared memory for such agents: research is recorded as an append-only directed acyclic graph (DAG) stored in Git, so that every claim is a commit anyone can check out and rerun. Each result, insight, hypothesis, verification, and report
recommendations.summary_zh: 本文提出 Agora，一個以 Git 作為共享記憶體的集體自動研究協調層。作者觀察到，自動研究代理若各自為政，每次 session 皆從零開始，增加代理只會帶來重複搜尋而非更多發現。Agora 將研究過程記錄為僅能附加的有向非循環圖：每項貢獻都是不可變的 Git commit，父邊代表「建立在何者之上」，並以衍生索引呈現研究前沿、被忽略的分支與驗證狀態，再以兼顧品質與多樣性的 UCB 規則分配注意力，防止社群塌縮為單一主流。論文報告首次長期實測：13 個語言模型代理在近 12 天、無中央規劃者的情況下，於權重轉移任務發表 1,703 項貢獻。任務要求在無訓練資料、無梯度更新的限制下，僅利用 141 個預訓練 donor 模型，初始化一個維度與任何 donor 都不匹配的 119.6M 參數注意力—SSM 混合模型。最佳結果將評估指標由隨機初始化的 3.39 降至 1.899 bits per byte，縮小 62% 與訓練過的 GPT-2 124M 之差距；勝出方法把 donor 的下個 token 統計壓縮進嵌入層與輸出頭，再對注意力、前饋與狀態空間區塊施加稀疏修改，其血統含 145 個 commit、橫跨 15 個帳號，並有 165 次獨立重現且無一失敗。限制包括：所有分數皆在同一開發評估器上挑選，缺乏與無 Agora 或純排行榜的對照組，因果效果未經檢驗；社群走出單一解的局部盆地有賴一次人為介入，作者亦未親自重跑勝出方法。本文的意義在於指出協調層而非個別代理才是擴展自動研究的瓶頸，並提出對照評估矩陣供後續量測。
recommendations.title: Agora: Git as Shared Memory for Collective AutoResearch
recommendations.title_zh: Agora：以 Git 作為集體自動研究的共享記憶體

links.title: DualSQL: Text-to-SQL with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

evidence: Abstract: DualSQL-4B reaches 68.0% execution accuracy on BIRD dev matching prior 7B models; DualSQL-8B reaches 71.1%, claimed SOTA for single-model solutions vs a 32B baseline (Arctic-Text2SQL-R1, Table 1).

Section 5.2.3 (Ablation Studies): under identical data/reward/hyperparameters, multi-turn agentic RL gains 2.3% EX and 5.4% REX over single-turn, and multi-agent RL adds a further 1.5% EX and 1.9% REX on BIRD-Dev.
Section 4.3 & Table 5: replacing EX with the proposed REX metric as reward raises single-agent 8B REX from 63.7 to 66.7 while EX moves 69.2 to 69.6, supporting the cleaner-reward claim.
Appendix D (Table 8): removing the SQL Execution tool drops SQL-generation EX by 2.5 points and REX by 6.8 points; every tool removal hurts, confirming the toolset ablation.
Section 5.1 (RL Setup): GRPO implemented on VeRL, lr 2e-6, batch 256, group 16, 32K token trajectory limit, Qwen3-4B/8B bases; Appendix B reports 4.5 days on 32 H100s for the 8B run.
Limitations section: restricted to read-only DB access, Qwen3 backbones only, REX acknowledged as an imperfect proxy reward; no code or checkpoint release is stated anywhere in the paper.
Section 5.2.2 (Table 4): out-of-domain Spider results (83.1 EX for DualSQL-8B vs 82.7 single-agent) show the recipe generalizes within SQLite text-to-SQL but only across these two benchmarks.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core-fit paper: multi-agent agentic RL (GRPO/VeRL) with a shared Qwen3 backbone and three DB tools for Text-to-SQL, directly matching Agents & Tool Use, Reasoning, Code, and RL preferences. Contribution is a sensible but incremental composition (joint schema-linking+SQL agents, rollout guardrails, new REX reward/metric) over existing RLVR text-to-SQL work it cites (e.g., MARS-SQL, Arctic-Text2SQL-R1). Rigor is above average: controlled single-turn vs single-agent vs multi-agent comparison on identical data/hyperparameters (Table 4), REX-vs-EX reward ablation (Table 5), guardrail ablation (Fig 2), per-tool ablation (Table 8), oracle-schema headroom analysis (Table 3), 8-run means with std. Caveats: headline baselines use different base models (Qwen2.5-Coder) than the paper's Qwen3, guardrail ablation rests on a single training-curve figure, manual error analysis is small-scale. Generalizability limited to SQLite/BIRD/Spider and Qwen3; no explicit code or checkpoint release statement, only hyperparameters, prompts, and REX pseudocode in appendices, so reproducibility is middling.

primary_link.title: DualSQL: Text-to-SQL with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

recommendations.summary: State-of-the-art Text-to-SQL systems are typically multi-agent pipelines centered around two fundamental tasks: schema linking and SQL generation. However, existing work trains separate models for each task, failing to leverage the synergy between these interrelated tasks. In this work, we propose DualSQL, a new Text-to-SQL system consisting of two agents powered by a single model backbone. The agents share the same model weights and agentic scaffold, enabling joint optimization through a robust
recommendations.summary_zh: 本文針對 Text-to-SQL（文字轉 SQL）系統中結構連結（schema linking）與 SQL 生成兩大核心任務長期被分開訓練、無法發揮協同效應的問題，提出 DualSQL 系統。該系統以單一共用參數的 Qwen3 開源模型為骨幹，同時驅動結構連結器與 SQL 生成器兩個代理，並配備 SQL 執行、全文檢索與資料庫剖析三種資料庫存取工具，使代理能透過多輪互動進行以資料庫為據的推理與驗證。訓練上採用多代理強化學習框架，並設計 rollout 護欄機制——嚴格格式檢查、rollout 中斷與損失遮罩——以穩定訓練、避免模式崩潰；另提出更嚴謹的 SQL 正確性指標 REX（robust execution match），修正傳統執行準確度 EX 對重複列與欄位順序的誤判。僅以 3755 筆 BIRD 訓練範例，DualSQL-4B 在 BIRD 開發集達 68.0% EX，媲美先前 7B 模型；DualSQL-8B 更達 71.1% EX，超越先前以 32B 參數建構的單一模型最佳方案，並在 Spider 測試集展現跨資料集泛化能力。消融實驗證實多代理聯合最佳化、REX 獎勵訊號與 rollout 護欄皆帶來顯著增益，工具消融則顯示 SQL 執行工具最為關鍵。限制方面，REX 仍屬 SQL 等價性的代理指標，可能產生誤判，獎勵設計亦缺乏細粒度的過程級訊號，且代理僅限唯讀資料庫存取。此研究證明聯合多代理強化學習是打造高效能 Text-to-SQL 系統的有效途徑，對以小型開源模型建構自然語言資料分析應用具重要意義。
recommendations.title: DualSQL: Text-to-SQL with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
recommendations.title_zh: DualSQL：以多代理強化學習進行文字轉 SQL

links.title: TAME: Token Attribution and Masking for Emergent misalignment

evidence: Abstract: attribution concentrated (top 5% of tokens hold 32% of mass); masking high-attribution tokens cuts EM 23x in Llama and 36x in Qwen; equal random mask leaves EM unchanged

Section 2, Stage 3: three conditions with identical text and hyperparameters (LoRA r=32, two epochs); random mask equalizes number of masked positions, not masked loss mass - confound acknowledged and deferred to Limitations
Section 3.2, Table 1: Llama full FT EM 8.6% [3.0,14.9] vs random mask 8.0% vs top 40% mask 0.4% [0.0,1.1]; Qwen 4.5%/6.4%/0.1%; factors computed from raw counts (69/800 vs 3/800; 36/800 vs 1/800)

Section 3.1: rarity controls - attribution-surprisal Spearman rho=0.68; register enrichment survives residualization in Llama (median 1.88x) but not Qwen (median 1.10x; 0.77x centered), so the characterization is scoped to Llama
Section 3.3, Table 2: held-out perplexity cost of top mask vs random mask is 3.7x on register tokens but only 1.3x on domain (medical) tokens, Qwen gradient 4.0/3.0/1.6/1.6x
Limitations: preliminary study with one domain (bad medical advice), one seed per training condition, small 1-1.5B students, single GPT-4o judge; 23x and 36x figures are single-run point estimates

Section 2 Setting: uses released Turner et al. (2025) bad-medical-advice organisms with public LoRA adapter and 6,849-example split; hyperparameters and lexicon (Appendix A) given, but the paper states no explicit code release for TAME itself
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM alignment/safety/interpretability work: token-level attribution and causal loss masking for emergent misalignment in Llama/Qwen fine-tuning, directly matching high-weight LLM, AI safety, alignment, and interpretability preferences. Novelty is solid: it moves EM localization from example/feature level to response-token level using released LoRA adapters (forward-pass-only scoring) and proposes an unwarranted-certainty register reading, though the technique itself is a simple interpolation derivative. Rigor is good with random-mask controls, surprisal quintile/residualization/centering controls, held-out perplexity decomposition, cross-family replication, and clustered bootstrap CIs, but undermined by single seeds, an untuned 40% mask, a count-not-loss-mass mask confound, and one GPT-4o judge - all honestly disclosed. Evidence strength benefits from large, CI-separated effects (8.6%->0.4% EM in Llama) and family replication; limited by single-run point estimates and judge-based scoring. Generalizability is moderate: one fine-tuning domain, small 1-1.5B students, and the register characterization fails the rarity control in Qwen (1.10x median), which the authors scope to Llama. Reproducibility is decent: public organisms/adapters, full lexicon in Appendix A, stated hyperparameters, but no explicit code release by the authors. Score: 0.4*0.9+0.15*0.75+0.15*0.7+0.15*0.7+0.1*0.6+0.05*0.6 = 0.77.

primary_link.title: TAME: Token Attribution and Masking for Emergent misalignment

recommendations.summary: Fine-tuning an aligned language model on narrow, flawed data can induce harmful behavior far outside the training domain, known as emergent misalignment (EM). Prior work has localized EM in model weights, activations, and training documents, but it remains unclear which training tokens carry the relevant fine-tuning signal. We introduce TAME (Token Attribution and Masking for Emergent Misalignment), a three-stage framework: token attribution scores how strongly the fine-tuning update raises each
recommendations.summary_zh: 當對齊後的語言模型在狹窄且有缺陷的資料上進行 fine-tuning，可能引發遠超出訓練領域的有害行為，即突現性失準。過往研究已將此現象定位於權重、激活與訓練文件層級，但究竟是哪些訓練詞元承載相關微調訊號仍不清楚。本文提出 TAME 三階段框架：第一階段沿著已釋出的 LoRA adapter 進行插值，僅用前向傳遞為每個回應詞元計算概似度提升的歸因分數；第二階段將高歸因詞元歸類為領域、語域、功能與其他，並以基底模型 surprisal 分位數控制詞元罕見度；第三階段在重新微調學生模型時對高歸因詞元施加損失遮罩，並以等量隨機遮罩作對照，完成因果驗證。在不良醫療建議的 model organisms 上，歸因高度集中（前 5% 詞元即佔 32% 質量）；Llama 的高歸因詞元在醫療詞彙上明顯匱乏，卻富含「完全」「安全」等表達不當確定性的語域，且在罕見度控制下依然成立。遮罩前 40% 高歸因詞元使 EM 率在 Llama 學生模型下降 23 倍、Qwen 下降 36 倍，等量隨機遮罩則幾無效果，困惑度代價集中於目標語域而非醫療內容。限制包括僅涵蓋單一領域、單一訓練種子、小型學生模型與單一 GPT-4o 評審，且語域富集現象在 Qwen 未能在罕見度控制下存續。本研究提示突現性失準或更取決於缺陷內容被表達的確定程度，而非內容本身，為不改動文字的資料稽核與防禦提供了廉價可行的切入點。
recommendations.title: TAME: Token Attribution and Masking for Emergent misalignment
recommendations.title_zh: TAME：以詞元歸因與遮罩探究突現性失準

links.title: Rational Clarification by Assistive Agents via Value-of-Information Reasoning

evidence: Section 1/Abstract: REVOIR decides ask-vs-act via cost-adjusted VoI of questions, formulated as a cooperative assistance game with user corrections, targeting LLM-based assistive agents.

Table I.1 (Appendix I.3): REVOIR (Factored + Incremental, ICL) reaches 58.8±0.4% PSR on seen and 56.0±3.5% on unseen personas vs Reflection-DPO 44.1±1.0% / 42.9±1.6%, using ~2.1 vs 9.8 questions, supporting the 13-15% and 5x-fewer-questions claims.

Section 4.1.1 and Fig. 2: REVOIR beats all ReAct variants in correctness under agent termination on Llama-3.1-70B and GPT-5.4-mini; reasoning-effort increases reduce ReAct clarifications, per Fig. 2 and Appendix D.2.
Appendix A, Props. A.1-A.2: Jensen-inequality proof that belief-adaptive best-of-K acting after clarification is never worse than acting immediately, with a finite-K epsilon/delta^K bound.

Appendix E: human validation of user simulator (72/89 agreement, 95% CI [0.72,0.88]) and LLM judge (41/57 agreement, CI [0.59,0.82]) on 9 annotators; small-sample but honestly reported with Wilson intervals.
Appendix D.3 (Figs. D.5-D.6): robustness to an unmodeled 'inattentive' user across p_dismissive 0.2-0.9, with ReAct baselines degrading.
Section 5 (Conclusion): acknowledged limitations — one-step myopic VoI, no dual control or interleaving, no real-user evaluation.

Appendices F, G, K: verbatim prompt templates, model versions (e.g., gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, GPT-4o-mini judge), tuned thresholds (Tables G.1-G.2), splits, and LoRA/ORPO details for the ReflectionDPO baseline; no explicit code-release claim found.
Table D.3: token-cost accounting showing SC-BoN-ReAct at K=20 uses ~74K tokens (>3x costliest REVOIR point) for marginal, non-monotonic correctness gains.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A methodology paper squarely on LLM assistive agents: inference-time value-of-information reasoning for ask-vs-act clarification, evaluated on ambiguous QA and preference-aligned planning against prompting, CoT/ReAct, self-consistency, EIG, and fine-tuned clarification baselines. High preference relevance (LLM agents, inference-time reasoning, alignment via assistance games, ICL) but not maximal because it is an application of established VoI/assistance-game machinery rather than a new model or training method; novelty is solid but incremental (cost-adjusted VoI over EIG and user-correction handling are the main new twists). Rigor is strong: formal A-POMDP formulation with propositions, many baselines, ablations (joint vs factored beliefs, batch vs incremental updates), budget sweeps, inattentive-user robustness tests, and human validation of the simulator and judge. Evidence is quantitatively backed (Tables D.1-D.2, I.1, token accounting D.3), though it rests on LLM-simulated users, a small human study, reproduced (not re-run) ADAPT baselines, and LLM-judged correctness; variance on unseen personas is high for joint variants. No code release is stated, capping reproducibility despite unusually thorough prompt/hyperparameter appendices. Limitations (one-step myopia, no dual control, no real users) are honestly stated.

links.title: RiskChainBench: A Benchmark for Obfuscated Platform Message Restoration and Evidence-Grounded Web Investigation

evidence: Abstract: 'Across ten models, Entry Top-1 ranges from 35.2% to 95.2% and web decision accuracy from 26.3% to 62.8%' and 'Execution failures account for 31.9% of web runs, whereas post-decision type errors account for only 0.9%'

Sec. 3.1 (Human construction of website gold): 'First-pass decision and joint-label agreement are 82.50% and 80.17%, with nominal Krippendorff's alpha of 0.6553 and 0.7425' and 'Hidden repeats yield 97.9% decision agreement'
Sec. 4.1 (Metrics): 'Primary metrics use central 95% intervals from 2,000 website-level bootstrap resamples... because each model-website pair is run once, they do not estimate rerun variance'
Conclusion (Sec. 5): 'The results use one trajectory per model-website pair... Future work should measure rerun variance... and validate the evidence rubric through a frozen human trajectory audit'

Sec. 3.4 (Multidimensional multimodal evidence judge): judge 'does not receive website annotations, model identity, URLs or domain-reputation signals' and 'does not determine the website decision or violation type'; evidence scores are 'coverage-conditioned' diagnostics only
Sec. 1: 'We release the benchmark, evaluation protocol, and resettable local sandbox, which also supports subsequent agent-training research'

Sec. 4.1 (Data and systems): 'Gemini 3.6 Flash is unranked in Task 2 because it was absent from the frozen report and judge batches'; Tables 1-2 report Task 1, Task 2, and gated end-to-end accuracies (16.7%-60.8%) for ten systems
llm_evaluation.rationale: An LLM/VLM agent benchmark that directly matches core preferences: web-agent investigation (Agents & Tool Use, 2.5), evaluation of ten frontier LLMs (LLMs, 2.5), platform-abuse risk detection (AI Safety 2.0; Red Teaming & Evaluation 1.8), and Chinese obfuscated-text restoration (NLP 1.5). Novelty is solid: the cross-stage 'entry-gated' composition linking message restoration to downstream web investigation is a formulation prior obfuscation and web-agent benchmarks lack (Sec. 1-2). Rigor is substantial but not exemplary: careful human gold construction with reported Krippendorff's alpha and hidden-repeat checks (Sec. 3.1), bootstrap CIs (Sec. 4.1), and clean protocol definitions (Sec. 3.4) are offset by a single trajectory per model-website pair, an unvalidated automated evidence judge, and key details (stratified results, judge rubric, construction audits) deferred to a supplement not present here; ablations are limited to failure-stage attribution. Evidence is strong for the headline claims (Entry Top-1 35.19-95.22%, web accuracy 26.3-62.8%, execution failures 31.9% vs 0.9% typing errors; Table 1, Fig. 5) but CIs and coverage details are in the supplement, and one model (Gemini 3.6 Flash) is inconsistently excluded from Task 2. Generalizability is moderate: fully synthetic Chinese-centric messages and offline-constructed sites limit transfer. Reproducibility is aided by an explicit release claim of benchmark, protocol, and resettable sandbox (Sec. 1, Conclusion), though verification depends on unseen supplementary material.

primary_link.title: RiskChainBench: A Benchmark for Obfuscated Platform Message Restoration and Evidence-Grounded Web Investigation

recommendations.summary: Platform abuse campaigns conceal redirection instructions with emojis, homophones, character decomposition, and redundant symbols, then route users through disguised links to services associated with pornography, fraud, gambling, or illicit transactions. Existing benchmarks evaluate obfuscated text and risky webpages separately, obscuring how target recovery affects downstream evidence acquisition. We introduce RiskChainBench, pairing 3,600 synthetic token-text restoration inputs from 600 source

llm_evaluation.rationale: In-scope LLM methodology paper (code agents, RLVR, reward shaping, LoRA joint training) with unusually thorough evaluation design: eight benchmark views, eight baselines with matched budgets (B3 given K=16 rollouts to equalize sandbox calls, §4.1), three-seed paired bootstrap CIs excluding zero (Table 3), component-wise ablations (Table 4), calibration/reliability metrics (Table 5), and inference-budget Pareto analysis (Table 6). recommendations.summary_zh: 執行回饋對程式碼模型是客觀的監督訊號，但整個程式常被壓縮成單一通過或失敗位元，使RLVR面臨困難的信用分配（credit assignment）問題；提示式審查者雖提供語言回饋，卻未與執行結果校準。ExecuCritic據此提出讓程式碼撰寫者與評論者共用凍結骨幹、各掛LoRA adapter、於同一批執行rollout上共同訓練的框架：評論者預測通過機率、排序候選並輸出簡短診斷；撰寫者採用校準優勢，僅當評論者分數與執行器結果在該rollout群組內的秩相關為正時，才將其納入GRPO優勢，避免採信不可信的獎勵。評論者損失結合判決似然、通過與失敗程式的排序邊際，以及對應執行器錯誤類型的診斷一致性。在Qwen3-8B與DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite上，橫跨HumanEval+、LiveCodeBench、SWE-bench Lite等八項基準，平均超越單一撰寫者GRPO約3.4點、提示式審查系統約6至7點，以約40%更少的策略梯度步數達到基線最終準確率，每個解決任務的沙盒執行次數由18.6降至10.7，patch排序的NDCG@5提升11.1點。消融顯示增益主要來自校準閘門、排序邊際與診斷一致性，而非更大的取樣預算；限制在於每個訓練提示皆需可執行的測試oracle，較弱或分布外的骨幹可能需更長的SFT階段。其價值在於以可驗證訊號錨定學得的密集回饋，在不淪為不可信獎勵模型的前提下，同時改善稀疏獎勵下的信用分配與樣本效率。

llm_evaluation.rationale: Strong topical match: a controlled study of LLM agents' in-context learning mechanisms (GPT-5, Qwen3-Plus) in multi-agent games, directly probing whether ICL reflects recursive reasoning or statistical extrapolation. The diagnostic is genuinely novel: exploiting the history-independence of rational expectations equilibrium (Section 2.2) to disentangle mechanisms by reordering identical price sets (Section 3.2). Rigor is solid - hypotheses H0/H1 are falsifiable, the game has a proven unique equilibrium (Appendix A), and full-sample analysis uses 7,800 observations with fixed effects, Yeo-Johnson transformation, and HC3 robust SEs (Appendix B.2). To disentangle these mechanisms, we study LLM agents in multi-agent incomplete-information games that require recursive belief reasoning. By constructing a public goods game and manipulating the statistical structure of historical feedback, we evaluate
recommendations.summary_zh: 這篇論文探究大型語言模型（LLM）代理在多代理相互依賴決策中的 in-context learning（ICL），究竟源自內部遞迴信念推理，或僅是對歷史統計模式的外推。作者以重複的 n 人公共財賽局為實驗平台，並引入理性預期均衡（REE）作為與歷史無關的理性基準：理論上最適門檻策略僅取決於當期公開成本與賽局基本結構，與歷史序列排列無關。實驗系統性操弄兩個面向——策略相互依賴強度 β（0.25 與 0.75）與回饋序列的統計結構（單調 vs. 跳躍式），並改變上下文長度（k=0、3、6 輪），以 GPT-5 與 Qwen3-Plus 驗證。主要證據顯示：當價格序列呈清晰單調趨勢時，加入歷史能大幅降低均衡偏離指標 ED，並使迴歸斜率趨近理論值 −10；一旦趨勢被跳躍序列破壞，較長上下文的效益幾乎消失，決策品質退化至無歷史基準，且高 β 會顯著放大此失敗。此結果支持 ICL 在此類策略環境中主要運作為統計外推，而非朝均衡方向的遞迴信念更新。限制包括僅測試兩個模型家族、單一賽局結構、較短上下文、純行為面分析與固定提示格式。本研究的價值在於將 REE 的歷史無關性轉化為區分推理與外推的診斷工具，並提供可重複調整參數的實驗框架，有助於刻劃 LLM 遞迴推理能力的邊界。

Section 6.4, Table 5: seeded random-proposer control sustains 3 of 20 usable iterations vs 11 and 14 for the LLM arms at $0 API cost
Section 6.5, Table 6: SGLang ngram speculative decoding sustains 1.2561x (run 1) and 1.2753x (extension) over its own frozen default across 18 ngram measurements
Section 6.7: graduated 11.03x gelu variant reads 0.79x against a re-derived Apple MLX baseline, reported as held-out non-transfer

llm_evaluation.rationale: Strongly on-topic: a measurement-integrity benchmark for LLM-agent auto-tuning of serving engines (vLLM/SGLang), touching agents, LLM inference/serving, evaluation methodology, reward hacking, and kernel code generation. Novelty is solid: making trust 'architectural' (protocol-as-code with test-enforced provenance, DB-level ingest rejection, anti-cheat gates outside the agent's modification surface, pre-registered readouts, external anchoring) is a fresh framing versus generator-centric systems (KernelBench, Astra, Sakana), though it inherits classical autotuning norms (OpenTuner/Ansor) and benchmark-integrity practice. Rigor is high for a systems benchmark: pre-registered A/B with treatment-delivery checkpoints, a seeded random-proposer control (Table 5), 53/53 re-measurement reproduction with 0.60% median deviation, digest-pinned engines, and ~290 regression tests; honest reporting of a required-n failure (11/14 usable vs bar of 15, §6.2) and a failed 1.2x median-speedup bar strengthens credibility. Evidence strength is tempered: all GPU results come from one box (DGX Spark GB10, §6), external anchoring lands in-band on only 1 of 5 cells with the rest explained post hoc (§6.1, Table 2), and the headline positive (SGLang 1.2561x/1.2753x, Table 6) is from one 7B model on a small flag space. Generalizability is limited by single-box scope, and the paper's own held-out device retest (§6.7: 11.03x certified on GB10 reads 0.79x on Apple MLX) demonstrates non-transfer, which it honestly frames as a protocol feature. Reproducibility is strong: released code/corpus at a tagged repo (footnote 1), frozen protocol file, pinned engine digests, paired seeds, ledgered costs (~$4.35 total), and audit trail.

Section 5.2 / Figure 10: gain decomposition by call length, 'reaching 34.2% and 35.3% at ten seconds or more'; per-phase ablation attributes remaining oracle gap mostly to uncovered channels (63% vs 17% recovery).
Limitations: paper itself bounds scope — remote APIs that 'answer only at the end', human-in-the-loop waits, and unparsable outputs are outside the census; 'coverage' is named as the limiting factor.

llm_evaluation.rationale: Core-fit agentic serving paper: tool-call progress reporting for KV cache management squarely matches the top-weighted preferences (Agents & Tool Use, Inference & Serving, Long Context & Memory), with coding-agent workloads and MCP hooks as secondary fits. Novelty is solid but bounded: the central insight is an acknowledged transfer of database progress-indicator lessons (Chaudhuri et al. 2004/2005) to LLM serving, with the first serving-side consumer and first tool-call progress census as genuine additions. Rigor is strong in structure — four reimplemented published baselines (Continuum, CacheWise, TokenCake, InferCept), oracle bound, controlled load-condition replays, per-phase ablation, cross-model checks, and bootstrap intervals for agent cost (Table 4) — but evaluation is replay-based on one 4xH100 setup, headline TTFT gains lack variance/repetition reporting, and controller thresholds are under-specified. Evidence is concrete and multi-point (median error ~1/5 vs ~1/3 of duration at 50%, <10% vs 80% at 90%; 20.7%/20.8% p90 TTFT cut vs 23% oracle), though the adversarial-lying analysis is self-described as preliminary. Generalizability is limited by the paper's own census: remote-API and human-wait calls are unreadable, coverage rather than precision is the binding constraint, and validation is coding-agent-centric despite a model-agnostic harness. Reproducibility is middling: methods, instruments, corpora, and the vLLM patch (Appendix D) are described in detail, but no artifact or code release is stated.

Appendix B.2, Table 8: true kernel 62.32 vs permuted kernel 61.15 vs identity kernel 60.85 on GSM8K (Qwen2.5-1.5B), supporting the geometry contribution

Appendix B.7, Tables 15-16: best results under both DeepSeek-V4-Pro and GLM-5.2 judges with positive paired-bootstrap 95% CIs against Top-W, p-less, Top-H
Appendix B.4, Table 11: end-to-end GPU latency increase ~5.8% (Qwen2.5-1.5B) and ~1.5% (Qwen3-4B); Table 4 reports 2.7x-7.4x lower CPU sampling overhead than Top-W
Limitations: static (non-contextual) token embeddings, diversity not always highest among decoders, and subset-size rule may not be optimal for all distributions
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM inference methodology: a plug-and-play decoding scheme (ME-Decoding) recasting token selection as Mahalanobis-distance ensemble pruning, evaluated on LLMs (Qwen3-4B, Phi-4-mini, Mistral-7B) for reasoning (GSM8K, GPQA) and open-ended generation (MT-Bench, AlpacaEval) - strongly aligned with LLM, reasoning, and inference/serving preferences. Novelty is moderate: geometry-aware and entropy-adaptive decoders (Top-W, CraEG, Top-H, Min-p, p-less) already exist; the ensemble-pruning lens and adaptive-bandwidth kernel are a fresh but incremental framing, and the greedy algorithm is acknowledged as OMP-related. Rigor is above average: Theorems 3.1-3.2 give unimodality and spectral approximation guarantees with full proofs (Appendix A), kernel ablations (identity/permuted, Table 8), component ablations (Table 9), matched probability-only controls (Table 5), lambda sweep (Table 12), 512/512 empirical unimodality (Table 10), and two-judge evaluation with paired bootstrap CIs (Appendix B.7). Gains are consistent but modest (GSM8K avg 72.66 vs 70.62 for Top-W, Table 2; GPQA 32.96 vs 31.56, Table 3) and baselines win several individual settings, tempering evidence strength. Theory rests on an unverified sufficient condition (kappa_N(K) <= 1 + lambda*H). Generalizability limited to <=7B models and short-form generation; authors flag contextualized kernels and long-form/multi-sample settings as future work. Reproducibility is good: public code link, specified hyperparameters (lambda=0.9, N=512), seeds, and hardware (Appendix B).

primary_link.title: Beyond Truncation: Rethinking LLM Decoding as Ensemble Pruning

recommendations.summary: We introduce Mahalanobis-Ensemble Decoding (ME-Decoding), a novel Large Language Model (LLM) decoding framework that frames candidate token selection as ensemble pruning. Existing selection strategies rely predominantly on scalar probabilities, ignoring geometric semantic relationships and causing candidate redundancy. Meanwhile, current geometry-aware methods often require complex optimization or directly reweighting the original token probabilities, leading to significant computational overhea
recommendations.summary_zh: 本文探討 LLM 解碼策略的核心限制：Top-k、Top-p、Min-p 等方法僅依賴純量機率截斷，將候選 token 視為獨立結果，忽略嵌入空間的語意幾何結構，造成候選冗餘；現有幾何感知方法則需複雜最佳化或重加權，帶來運算負擔或不穩定。作者提出 Mahalanobis-Ensemble Decoding（ME-Decoding），把逐步 token 選擇類比為集成學習的剪枝問題：機率對應個別準確度，嵌入相似度對應冗餘度。方法定義 Mahalanobis 距離驅動的 MEE 能量，結合依據 Tsallis 熵調整的規模懲罰構成 MES 目標；相似度矩陣以自適應頻寬的高斯核於正規化嵌入上建構。針對此 NP-hard 問題，作者設計貪婪前向選擇演算法，增量維護反 Cholesky 因子，提前停止下複雜度近似線性於候選數，並證明路徑單峰性與近似保證。實驗於 Qwen3-4B、Phi-4-mini 與 Mistral-7B 上，ME-Decoding 在 GSM8K、GPQA 平均準確度與 MT-Bench、AlpacaEval 皆取得最佳平均表現；CPU 抽樣開銷比 Top-W 快約 2.7 至 7.4 倍，GPU 端到端延遲僅增約 1.5% 至 5.8%。限制包括相似度矩陣採靜態嵌入、難以捕捉上下文語意，多樣性未必最高，最佳子集大小仍不易決定。整體而言，此研究提供免訓練、即插即用的推論時解碼新典範。
recommendations.title: Beyond Truncation: Rethinking LLM Decoding as Ensemble Pruning
recommendations.title_zh: 超越截斷：從集成剪枝觀點重新思考 LLM 解碼

links.title: A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment

evidence: Abstract & Section 1: ComPO is a zeroth-order alignment method using comparison oracles to extract signal from low-margin ('noisy') preference pairs without optimizing a differentiable preference loss, motivated by likelihood displacement.

Theorem 3.2 (Section 3.1) and Appendix B.2: best-iterate convergence guarantee under ℓ-smoothness, approximate gradient sparsity (‖∇f‖₁≤√s‖∇f‖), and oracle compatibility with a latent objective f—assumptions the paper admits are theoretical benchmarks, not practical criteria (Remark 3.3).
Section 4.3 / Algorithm 4 discussion: the length-normalized statistic (Eq. 14) and soft damping (Eq. 15) are heuristics; the text states Algorithm 4 'cannot be covered by Theorem 3.4'.

Table 1 (Section 4.1): DPO_clean+ComPO raises AlpacaEval 2 LC (Mistral-7B-Instruct 24.14→26.17; Llama-3-8B-Instruct 32.92→35.79) but Arena-Hard drops 14.4→10.5 for Mistral-7B-Instruct, attributed only speculatively to raw-WR length bias (avg length 513 vs 468).

Tables 4-7 (Section 4.2): ablations over perturbation count m (800-5400), perturbed layers, entry threshold λ_g (best at ~1-6% entries retained), and noisy-pair count (100→300) report mean±std over five runs.
Section 4.1: experiments use UltraFeedback, hyperparameters (δ_margin=3, r, m=1600-1800, λ_g, λ=0.2) and 30 NVIDIA A40 GPUs are specified; no public code release is mentioned.
Table 10 (Section 4.3): online damping and replay improve metrics (e.g., Qwen3-4B-Base AE LC 16.20→17.43→18.57; Gemma-3-4B-it Arena-Hard 57.7→63.3→63.7) over offline ComPO.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Directly in-scope: an LLM preference-alignment method (ComPO) targeting likelihood displacement in DPO-style direct alignment, squarely matching LLM and Alignment/RLHF preferences. The zeroth-order comparison-oracle mechanism is adapted from 1-bit compressed sensing (SCOBO/Sign-OPT) rather than invented, and comparison/ranking oracles for RLHF already exist (Tang et al. 2024b; Zhang & Ying 2025), so novelty is moderate; the online extension reuses the coverage analysis of Song et al. (2024b). Rigor is solid: two theorems with proofs (Theorems 3.2, 3.4, Appendix B), but they rest on a latent smooth sparse-gradient oracle-compatibility assumption that is unverifiable, and the practical schemes (output-layer-only perturbation, entry thresholding, length-normalized damping) are acknowledged to fall outside the theory (Section 4.3 states the practical online scheme 'cannot be covered by Theorem 3.4'). Evidence is mixed: consistent LC gains across five model families (Tables 1, 3, 10) with five-run ablations reporting mean±std, but main tables are single-run point estimates, judge models switch between GPT-4 Turbo and GPT-4.1 across tables, and a clear regression is unexplained beyond length confounds (Arena-Hard 14.4→10.5 for Mistral-7B-Instruct, Table 1). The pair-level likelihood diagnostics (Table 2) cover only two models. Hyperparameters, datasets, checkpoints, and hardware are documented, but no code release is stated, limiting reproducibility for an m=1600-1800, 30-GPU method.

primary_link.title: A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment

recommendations.summary: Direct preference alignment methods are widely used to align large language models (LLMs) with human preferences because of their computational and memory efficiency. However, likelihood displacement motivates alternative ways to extract information from preference pairs with small likelihood margins. In this paper, we propose and analyze Comparison-based Preference Optimization (ComPO), a zeroth-order alignment method based on comparison oracles. ComPO extracts directional information from thes
recommendations.summary_zh: 直接偏好對齊方法（如 DPO）雖具計算與記憶體效率，但存在 likelihood displacement（似然位移）問題：當偏好對中偏好與不偏好回應在模型度量下相似、似然邊際極小時，直接以固定邊際損失最佳化，可能降低偏好回應的絕對機率，造成非預期的未對齊。作者提出 ComPO，一種基於比較神諭的零階對齊方法：不對這類 noisy 偏好對最佳化可微分損失，而是擾動目前政策，檢驗擾動是否同時提高偏好回應似然並降低不偏好回應似然，再將一位元比較信號聚合為正規化更新方向；實作上僅擾動輸出層權重並做逐項門檻化。線上版本進一步利用未標記的政策生成，以 reverse-KL 代理量阻尼步長並搭配重播緩衝區。理論上，在平滑性、梯度稀疏性與神諭相容假設下證明離線方案的最佳迭代收斂保證，並在精確 reverse-KL 限制與局部覆蓋條件下建立線上性能界。實驗於 Mistral、Llama-3、Gemma-2、Qwen3、Gemma-3 進行，ComPO 接在 DPO 或 SimPO 之後多半提升 AlpacaEval 2 LC、Arena-Hard 與 MT-Bench 表現，成對似然診斷與緩解似然位移一致；僅更新約 1% 輸出層參數，GPU 記憶體峰值遠低於 DPO。限制包括理論假設潛在目標與稀疏梯度未必成立、實務啟發式（長度正規化阻尼、重播）未被理論涵蓋，且 Mistral 在 Arena-Hard 原始勝率反而下滑。本工作顯示小邊際偏好對仍蘊含可用資訊，透過比較信號安全地擷取，可作為現有直接對齊方法的模組化補充。
recommendations.title: A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment
recommendations.title_zh: LLM 偏好對齊的零階典範

links.title: SYNCR: Diagnosing and Learning Cross-Video Reasoning from Simulation

evidence: Sec. 3.2 / Table 1: 22 MLLMs evaluated; best standard open-weight average 37.5% (Qwen3-VL 32B); GPT-6 Astra 64.5% vs human majority vote 89.5% on matched 100-item sets.

Sec. 4.1 / Fig. 4 and Table 9: eight-task SFT raises Qwen3-VL-8B from 32.6% to 61.6% average on matched 200-item sets; GRPO from base yields only +2.5 to +4.2 points under the tested binary-reward configuration.
Sec. 4.3 / Table 20: ordering gains of +9.0/+19.0 (Qwen3-VL-8B), +14.0/+20.5 (InternVL3.5-8B), +19.0/+16.5 (Qwen3-VL-4B) on Assembly101/Panoptic with exact McNemar p<=0.015 or conservative bounds.

App. C.4.2 / Table 15: format-matched placebo trained on identical inputs with wrong labels scores below base on every SYNCR and real-benchmark task (e.g., MVU-Eval TR 43.0% vs base 68.0%, SFT 75.5%).
App. C.4.1 / Table 14: matched-budget SAT supervision arm does not reproduce gains (-8.5 and -17.0 points on MVU-Eval TR and CrossVid PSS vs +7.5 and +10.0 for SYNCR SFT).

App. C.4.5: Benjamini-Hochberg correction; seven of eight SYNCR task gains and both existing temporal-benchmark transfer gains survive; Thinking-checkpoint comparisons do not survive and are explicitly not treated as findings.

App. B.3.2 / Table 8: SYNCR averages correlate with MVU-Eval TR and Comparison (Spearman rho 0.855/0.917, p<0.001; 0.779/0.870 after partialling log10 params), with the caveat that a general video factor could explain this.

Reproducibility statement / App. C.1: evaluation and training metadata plus Habitat/Kubric assets released at huggingface.co/datasets/CrossVideoReasoning/SYNCR; LoRA (rank 16, alpha 32, lr 5e-5) and GRPO hyperparameters fully specified; CLEVRER videos must be obtained separately.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A simulator-grounded cross-video reasoning benchmark plus paired training study for multimodal LLMs. It matches high-weight preferences on LLMs/MLLMs, (visual) reasoning, multimodal AI, benchmark evaluation, SFT/LoRA training and GRPO-style RL, though it is video-centric rather than core text-LLM work and touches none of the top-preference agent/Japanese-NLP/safety topics. Novelty is solid: Table 3 shows no prior multi-video benchmark couples simulator-state labels, matched training QA, evidence controls, and post-training transfer tests, but simulation-based supervision for video MLLMs has precedent (SAT, SIMS-V, Chain-of-Frames). Rigor is exceptional: Wilson intervals, exact McNemar tests, Benjamini-Hochberg correction, three training seeds, format-matched placebo, matched-budget SAT arm, no-video/single-video controls, and timestamp-leakage prevention, with unusually careful hedging of weak results (e.g., cross-camera counting transfer 'not established'). Evidence is strong for the headline claims (SFT 32.6%->61.6% on matched 200-item sets; ordering transfer +9.0 to +20.5 pts with p<=0.015), with honest limitations (proprietary models on only 100 items/task, correlation with MVU-Eval does not establish construct isolation, 4-person majority-vote human reference). Generalizability is decent since structural/camera-rig/simulator shifts are tested, but transfer beyond ordering is mixed and only three model families and multiple-choice visual-only inputs are covered. Reproducibility is good: public HuggingFace release, full hyperparameters (App. C.1), prompt templates, and statistical protocol, with CLEVRER requiring third-party access.

links.title: SPLASH: Switching Parallel Layouts of Attention with Seamless Handoff for LLM Serving

evidence: Abstract: 'Splash improves end-to-end serving throughput by 1.3–1.73× over fixed-layout deployments' on B200 serving GLM-5.3; open source at https://github.com/ict-agent/SPLASH-sglang.
§5.5/Table 1: all twelve directed switches at B=16, 256K context; Splash overhead 0.02–11.76 ms p50 vs blocking up to 667.31 ms; median overhead under 0.51% of target-ready.
§5.3/Table 3: DOP holds 8,271,360 distinct KV tokens vs 6,497,792 for DP-attention (27.3% more) on B200 at memory fraction 0.85.

Appendix B.1: 'These are one parameterization of Equation 10... The coefficients specify assumed utilization, communication, and overlap, rather than measured rates' — DCU/H200 latency models are illustrative, and H200 pool sizes are 'analytical projections... not measurements'.

Appendix G (Limitations): graph capture per layout, memory headroom for one-layer buffers, imperfect overlap for long-history switches, short-lived regimes, and DOP transfer path requiring 'equal TP and attention-DP degrees with one rank per owner'.
Appendix C: implementation built atop SGLang 0.5.10 with sparse FlashMLA backend; experiments on Vast.ai-rented B200/H200 and BW1000 DCUs; each sweep point averages 10 runs.

§6: acknowledges Pope et al. (2023) 'shard multiquery attention over the batch on TPUs to avoid replicating its KV head', positioning DOP's novelty specifically against DP-attention replicas for absorbed MLA.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A systems paper on live-switching attention parallel layouts (TP/CP/DP-attention/new DOP) for LLM serving, squarely aligned with high-weight preferences: LLM serving (Abstract: 'improves end-to-end serving throughput by 1.3–1.73× over fixed-layout deployments' for GLM-5.3/DeepSeek-V3.2), long context & KV cache, inference & serving (SGLang 0.5.10 base), and efficiency; agentic/RL-rollout workloads motivate but are not the contribution. Novelty is solid but bounded: the ownership-model framing is clean and DOP is claimed new ('to our knowledge, a new layout', §1), though the paper itself concedes Pope et al. (2023) already sharded MQA KV over the batch (§6), so DOP is chiefly novel for absorbed MLA. Rigor is strong for a systems paper (formal footprint/switch equations §2-3, per-layer primitive timings §5.4, full 128/136/116-measurement tables §D, honest negatives like DOP trailing CP by 42.2% at 128K/B=1, limitations Appendix G), but the abstract's headline 1.3–1.73× follow-the-layout claim is not backed by an explicit dynamic-workload (e.g., rollout trace) experiment, the DCU/H200 latency models are admitted 'illustrative timing law[s]' with assumed coefficients (Appendix B.1), and no empirical comparison against prior reconfiguration systems (Flying Serving, Shift Parallelism) is run. Evidence for switch overheads is strong (0.02–11.76 ms p50 vs up to 667.31 ms blocking, Table 1; 27.3% more KV capacity, Table 3), but end-to-end scheduling benefits are inferred from fixed-layout sweeps. Generalizability is decent—three hardware platforms and three models show consistent regimes—yet DOP's gains are specific to head-free MLA caches and the transfer path requires equal TP/attention-DP degrees (Appendix G). Reproducibility is good: open-source implementation, detailed configuration appendices, seeds, and 10-run averaging, though reproducing requires renting B200/H200/DCU hardware and frontier models.

links.title: AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation

evidence: Abstract: 'Experiments with Qwen3-8B advisors for Gemini and Claude show that AdviSD outperforms advisor-GRPO by 4.2-6.4 percentage points on BFCL-v3 and by 3.9-5.1 score points on EnvScaler.'
Section 7 (Q2), Table 2: 'AdviSD exceeds matched-count random selection by 2.5-4.9 points and no gating by 3.2-5.1', while 'AdviSD, inverted gate' trails GRPO on both benchmarks with both executors.

Section 4.2, Theorem 1: 'Decreasing r_I/r_S strictly increases both theta* and J(theta*)'; Section 6/Corollary 1 motivates the matched-count random control because uniform thinning 'changes exposure, not composition'.

Section 7 (Evaluation): 'Every trained method has three independent training runs... evaluate it four times on the test set, and average the four scores'; Appendix E notes no-advisor/frozen-advisor SDs 'reflect only evaluation randomness'.
Appendix E 'Scope and limitations': 'Evaluation covers two executor families, one shared reflector, and three runs per trained method. The updates to API models can constrain exact reproducibility.'

Appendix C.3 (end): 'AdviSD's predictive score does not guarantee mu_G > mu_0' and the results 'do not establish finite-run robustness to teacher noise or convergence for AdviSD with its evolving self-teacher and GRPO-AdamW updates'; Appendix E.1: observed retention decline 'does not identify those classes or rule out changes in score scale or in the proposal distribution'.

Appendix H.3: paired-contrast precedents (RLCSD, OCSD, PBSD, RLSD); 'AdviSD differs in the prediction target and the role of the contrast: the advisor scores a separate executor's recorded response with and without issued advice'.

Table 3 (Q3): OOD macro-averages 77.2 (Gemini) and 74.0 (Claude) lead compared methods; Section 7 notes 'AdviSD itself trails standalone execution and GRPO by 1.7% points on Claude's ACEBench multi-step tasks'.

Appendix D, Table 4 and Appendix F: full training configuration (4 H100 GPUs, 200 updates, lr 1e-6, YaRN factor 4, top-100 token support, lambda_s schedule, u_d=0.95) and exact executor/advisor/reflector/teacher prompts; but no release of the authors' own code is stated anywhere in the document.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Strongly in-scope: trains a small LLM advisor (Qwen3-8B) with GRPO plus selective feedback-conditioned self-distillation to steer frozen frontier LLM executors (Gemini, Claude) on multi-turn tool-use benchmarks, hitting LLM, agents/tool-use, and RL/alignment preferences directly. Novelty is moderate: advisor models, feedback-conditioned self-distillation (SDPO, DistIL, HERO, HinT-SD), and paired-contrast selection (RLCSD, OCSD, PBSD, RLSD) are acknowledged close precedents; the distinct contributions are applying paired with/without-advice scoring of a recorded executor response to gate advisor supervision, donor-advice threshold calibration, an abstention bypass, and a stylized two-teacher theory separating supervision composition from exposure. Rigor is solid: explicit assumptions and honest scoping of the theory (does not cover the actual changing-teacher GRPO-AdamW training and the gate is not shown to identify the theoretical sensitivity classes), fixed test sets, validation-based checkpoint selection, well-motivated ablations including a matched-count random control and inverted gate. Evidence is consistent across two executors, two in-domain and four OOD benchmarks plus cross-version/cross-family transfer, with honest negative notes (e.g., trails standalone on Claude ACEBench multi-step; transferred advisors underperform executor-specific training). Deductions: only three runs with SD but no significance tests, a single advisor model and reflector, known confound that the matched-count control runs on its own rollouts, closed API executors, and no code release for the method despite very detailed hyperparameters and prompts.
topics: agent benchmarks (BFCL-v3, EnvScaler, ACEBench, ToolHop, tau2-bench, RoTBench)

links.title: Orthogonal Yet Coupled: Decoupling Geometric Components for Model Merging

evidence: Abstract and Section 1: DiGA orthogonally decomposes task vectors into orientation and structural components and claims cross-component coupling is 'a previously overlooked interference'; repository stated as github.com/wzj1718/DiGA
Section 4.2 Table 1: DiGA reaches Task Avg. 59.18% (LoRA) and 58.60% (OFT) merging five Llama-3.1-8B experts, exceeding strongest baselines by 0.48 and 1.28 points
Section 4.2 Table 2 and Table 3: DiGA averages 41.09% on MergeBench fully fine-tuned Llama-3.2-3B experts (vs 40.87% best baseline) and 61.84% on three Qwen2.5-VL-7B experts (vs 61.66% best baseline)

Section 4.4 Table 5: component separation improves TIES/DARE/TSVM Task Avg. by +0.26/+0.56/+0.37, while Component-Joint reduces TSVM by 2.25 points; norm ratios near 1.0 indicate gains are directional, not magnitude-based
Appendix F.2 Table 7: Task Avg. 58.03±0.31 over all 120 expert orderings, with 118/120 orderings beating OrthoMerge
Appendix E: derivations and proofs of existence, uniqueness, and cross-component orthogonality of the base-induced decomposition

The orientation/structural orthogonal decomposition via QR of the base weight and the 'cross-component coupling' claim are genuinely new within the geometric merging line (TSVM, OrthoMerge, Iso-CTS), with supporting proofs in Appendix E. Rigor is solid: ablations (Table 4), generality tests over TIES/DARE/TSVM (Table 5), full 120-permutation ordering sensitivity (Table 7), and geometric analyses (Section 4.5), but the aggregation rule (gamma=(1+c_bar)*n_bar) is heuristic, gains are modest (0.18-1.28 points), no significance tests or seed variance for main results, and several ablation deltas are within noise margins. Evidence is consistent and multi-setting but small-magnitude; a weakness is that whole-vector ablation differs by only 0.36 points. Generalizability is shown across LoRA/OFT/full fine-tuning and language plus vision-language settings, but limited to transformer 2D projection matrices and 3B-8B scale. Reproducibility is strong: public code, Algorithm 1, fixed expert orderings, harness specifications (Appendix D), and hardware details.

links.title: Alpha Diffusion Language Models: Factorization Alone Is Not the Problem

evidence: Table 1 / Section 4.1: AlphaDLM (k=16) reaches 34.6% GSM8K at 4 NFE versus 4.2% for MDLM evaluated with the same fixed-NFE confidence sampler; other baselines at most 7.7% at 4 NFE.

Section 4.1 (Table 3): matched comparison from shared k=1 checkpoint at 250k updates — sequence-level k=16 34.65% vs best token-wise 19.86% at 4 NFE; k=8 49.20% vs 44.35% token-wise at 16 NFE; single training seed and EMA weights noted.

Section 3.2 / Appendix B, B.1: factorized optimum characterized as marginals of a distribution minimizing D_KL to lower-temperature target plus (alpha/(1-alpha))·TC, building on Lapidoth and Pfister (2019); Proposition 1 proved via arithmetic-geometric mean inequality, with boundary analysis at alpha=1/m and a counterexample showing the support condition is necessary.

llm_evaluation.rationale: Core language-model methodology paper squarely in scope: a new training objective (sequence-level generalized cross-entropy/alpha loss) for masked diffusion LMs, evaluated on math reasoning (GSM8K/MATH500) and code (HumanEval/MBPP), with low-NFE parallel decoding as the efficiency focus. Matches LLM (2.5), Training (1.5), Inference (1.5), Reasoning (2.5, indirectly via math benchmarks), and Code (2.0) preferences. Novelty is solid: the reframing that factorization alone is not the barrier, plus a characterization of the factorized optimum as marginals of a KL-vs-total-correlation solution, is fresh relative to trajectory-distillation and dependency-modeling approaches, though alpha loss itself and token-wise variants are known. Rigor is high: controlled objective ablations at shared initialization and sampler (Section 4.1), initialization sensitivity (Appendix E), ancestral and adaptive sampling controls, and detailed proofs with boundary cases and a counterexample (Appendix B.1). Evidence is strong for the headline claim (34.6% at 4 NFE vs 4.2% MDLM under the same sampler) but absolute accuracy remains below autoregressive references (53.9-63.3%), single training seed per recipe, gains shrink at higher NFE, and code results are mixed (peak accuracy highest for CE/CE+CAP across the full sweep, Section 4.2). Generalizability is demonstrated at two scales/settings but with per-setting k tuning. Reproducibility is aided by full recipes and documented baseline protocols, yet no code or checkpoint release is stated.

The method combines known ingredients (sparse autoencoders, relational GNNs, prefix conditioning) into a reasonably fresh query-conditioned latent graph formulation with an evidence-reconstruction anti-collapse objective. Evaluation is broad: 3 benchmarks, 3 backbones, ~15 baselines across 4 families, component ablations, efficiency frontiers, and a token-budget sweep. Main deductions: single fixed seed with no variance or significance testing; Table 1 mixes copied MemCoE numbers (*) with own runs, undermining protocol uniformity; fully fine-tuning the backbone on benchmark data is not matched by non-training baselines like Long Context/Naive RAG, potentially inflating gains; 'neuro-symbolic' framing is thin since no genuinely symbolic component exists; no code release statement despite exhaustive hyperparameter disclosure. Comparisons against official GPT-5/GPT-4.1 numbers on PersonaMem-v2 are fair but indirect.

recommendations.summary_zh: 個人化代理須在長期互動歷史中推理，才能同時掌握明確陳述的偏好與隱含的行為線索。既有做法或將記憶片段獨立評分而難以串連分散證據，或依賴與查詢無關的靜態圖，且原始文字記憶糾纏多雜訊，推理成本高昂。本文提出 LGM，將長期記憶解糾纏搬入連續潛在空間：彙整骨幹語言模型多層隱藏狀態，把每則互動與查詢映射為低維潛在節點，以稀疏自編碼器拆解為稀疏概念；邊權重由查詢與記憶的概念重疊決定，使同一記憶池在不同提示下形成不同拓撲；關聯式圖神經網路在活化子圖上傳遞訊號，讀出緊湊圖狀態並轉為少量潛在前綴 token 供生成條件化，再以證據重建損失防止表徵塌縮，全程端對端可微最佳化。實驗於 PersonaMem、PrefEval 與 PersonaMem-v2 隱含偏好子集，搭配 Qwen2.5-7B、Gemma3-4B、Qwen3-4B 骨幹：LGM 平均準確率達 72.28 與 66.16，領先最強基線 MemCoE 逾 11 個百分點；在 PersonaMem-v2 上以 4B 模型達 62.9（32K）與 51.9（128K），超越 GPT-5 系列閉源模型，且呼叫次數、token 消耗與首 token 延遲皆居低成本前沿；消融顯示證據重建最關鍵。限制：需端對端微調圖模組與骨幹，訓練成本較高，評估亦限於個人化基準。其價值在於證明按需在潛在空間組織記憶可兼顧準確與效率，為個人化代理指出新途徑。

llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM-methodology work on decoding for masked diffusion language models, evaluated on math reasoning (GSM8K, MATH500) and code generation (HumanEval, MBPP), squarely within preferred LLM/reasoning/code/inference topics. The training-free, geometry-aware (SLERP + MASK-norm) soft-token construction is a sensible, well-motivated contribution, though SLERP is a standard technique and concurrent work (Nigam et al.) uses spherical interpolation with training; the main differentiator is the frozen-model setting plus the agreement-seeking analysis. Rigor is solid: four DLMs, three parallelism settings, matched hyperparameter search for the baseline (Appendix A.2), ablations isolating interpolation rule vs. norm (Table 5), sensitivity analysis (Fig. 2), adaptive-sampler integration (Table 6), and recovery rates (Table 7). However, no seeds/error bars or significance tests are reported, some gains are small or reversed (e.g., LLaDA MATH500 at 2 tokens/step: ours 23.60 vs. vanilla 24.40, Table 2), and the mechanistic analysis relies on 70 controlled toy prompts with a self-derived reference, as acknowledged in the Limitation section. Evidence strength is good given consistency across models and the geometric measurements (89.42° separation, 0.863× norm shrinkage, Appendix B.1), but the analysis is diagnostic rather than validated against ground truth. Generalizability is limited to masked DLMs with RMSNorm; no autoregressive or non-RMSNorm models tested. Reproducibility is strong: public code, public models/benchmarks, specified shots, token limits, hyperparameters, and full prompt collection (Appendix D.5).
